title: Core Reliability Hardening
summary: Mitchell's core work moved forward: auth UI is reconciled against the one canonical session, Analyse/Packaging cannot inherit stale sign-in gates, and deep Packaging now rejects weak or generic outputs before they are shown or saved.
discord_changes: Hardened visible auth state against the single canonical Supabase session so stale sign-in-required UI cannot fight the real session.
Added a source-specificity rejection gate to deep Packaging: weak receipts, generic templates and near-duplicate options are blocked.
Kept Founder Weekly honest: browser auth proof and real AI Packaging outputs are still required before those checkpoints close.
changes: Added v295-core-hardening.js as a post-auth reliability layer after the focused v0.29.4 product cleanup.
Continuously reconciles the visible signed-in/signed-out state from window.YTIntelAuth, the canonical client created by v291-auth-core.
Keeps Analyse and Packaging inputs enabled and removes stale authentication-required errors from the signed-out core workflow.
Added YTIntelAuthDiagnostic() for deterministic production auth QA without exposing tokens or credentials.
Replaced the Packaging click path with a stricter v0.29.5 source contract while retaining the same deep v082 provider path.
Requires multiple source receipts, current-source citation, concrete source-anchor overlap, substantial hooks and materially distinct package territories.
Rejects generic title templates and refuses to render or save any package run that fails the client specificity gate.
Bumped the PWA shell to v0.29.5.
why_it_matters: The remaining Founder Weekly work is proof, not hand-waving. The app now has stronger code-level guarantees around the two unfinished critical areas while still refusing to award progress until real signed-in/signed-out browser evidence and three real source-specific Packaging outputs exist.
